subject: Arabic numerals
hook: ARABIC NUMERALS IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: Arabic numerals are not actually Arabic in origin; they were developed in North Africa and represent Western digits that evolved separately from the Eastern Arabic numerals used in the Middle East.
angle_support: The immediate ancestors of the digits now commonly called "Arabic numerals" were introduced to Europe in the 10th century by Arabic speakers of Spain and North Africa.
In the east from Egypt to Iraq and the Arabian Peninsula, the Arabs were using the Eastern Arabic numerals or Mashriqi numerals: ٠, ١, ٢, ٣, ٤, ٥, ٦, ٧, ٨, ٩.
title: Why Your Numbers Are Not Arabic
description: The digits we call Arabic numerals are not the same ones used in the Middle East. They were actually designed in North Africa and spread through Europe by trade.
narration: ARABIC NUMERALS IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture the digits we use daily as Middle Eastern inventions. It was closer to a North African design, distinct from the Eastern Arabic numerals used in Egypt. Known as Western digits or Ghubār numerals, these symbols were developed in the Maghreb. While the Middle East used a different set of ٠-٩ characters, European traders adopted the North African versions from the 10th century onwards. The numbers you write every day are actually Western Arabic digits.
